findings.title: Removed handling of rules deleted from ruler but still in Prometheus (and vice versa) causes inconsistent/stale UI
findings.body: The previous implementation fetched both ruler and Prometheus groups and reconciled them (matchRules), showing 'Creating'/'Deleting' operation states for rules that are out of sync between the two APIs. This PR removes the ruler fetch entirely and only renders based on the Prometheus response. As a result, rules that have just been created (visible in ruler but not yet in Prometheus) or deleted (removed from ruler but still present in Prometheus due to eventual consistency) will not show any transitional state, or will show rules as fully loaded/normal when they're actually deleting/creating, since there's no mechanism to detect this discrepancy anymore. This changes user-visible behavior and removes test coverage (GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx removed tests for 'Creating'/'Deleting' states) without an equivalent replacement, which could confuse users during rule creation/deletion.

findings.title: isPaused and provenance now derived from Prometheus data instead of ruler, potentially stale due to eventual consistency
findings.body: GrafanaRuleListItem now solely relies on `rule.isPaused` and `rule.provenance` from the GrafanaPromRuleDTO (Prometheus) rather than the ruler response (`grafana_alert.is_paused`/`provenance`). Since Prometheus endpoints are eventually consistent (per comments elsewhere in the codebase, e.g. the removed matchRules logWarning), pause state and provenance status shown in the UI may lag behind recent ruler-side changes (e.g. right after pausing/unpausing a rule), leading to incorrect state being displayed temporarily, with no mechanism to reconcile this discrepancy.

findings.title: Missing key prop on GrafanaRuleListItem elements in list
findings.body: In the switch statement, the 'grafana' case renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` without a `key` prop, while the other cases (`datasource`, `default`) correctly pass `key={key}`. Since this is inside `.map()`, React will warn about missing keys and reconciliation may behave incorrectly (e.g., unnecessary remounts) for Grafana-origin rules in the filtered list.

findings.title: Delete menu item unavailable when only promRule is provided (list view)
findings.body: The Delete menu item is gated on `canDelete && rulerRule`, requiring a rulerRule to be present. However, per the new doc comment, consumers coming from the alert list view only pass `promRule` (ruler API calls have been removed from that view), meaning `rulerRule` will be undefined and the Delete action will never render for Grafana rules in the list view, even though `canDelete` may be derived correctly from the Grafana Prometheus rule abilities. This silently breaks the delete workflow from the new list view for users who otherwise have permission.

findings.title: Silence drawer gated on rulerRule, won't trigger for promRule-only consumers
findings.body: `showSilenceDrawer` rendering is conditioned on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`, requiring the ruler rule. Since the component now also supports promRule-only usage (per RuleProps using RequireAtLeastOne and the new grafana prom ability checks), when only `promRule` is supplied (as in the new list view), the Silence button triggered via AlertRuleMenu's `handleSilence` sets `showSilenceDrawer` to true but the drawer will never actually render because `rule` (rulerRule) is undefined, silently breaking the silence action for list-view-only consumers.
